ranking.rationale: Strongest candidate: the only directly screened feature group with positive overall lift, full coverage, low leakage and runtime risk, and a tightly controlled ablation. Its modest expected gain is supported by the best available evidence.
Temporal context has positive lifts on three of four days and isolates a plausible portion of the winning group. It is narrower than c01 but carries medium leakage and temporal-regime risk.
Very feasible and low risk, with clean isolation of tab, but evidence is only inherited from the aggregate request-context result and the expected gain and confidence are lower than c03.
Offers meaningful nonlinear-capacity upside without new feature leakage, but evidence is weak, confidence is low, and architecture replacement introduces overfitting and runtime risk.
Directly targets nDCG improvement and is interesting, but loss changes are broad, runtime risk is high, leakage and candidate-group integrity concerns remain, and GAUC may decline.
Potentially useful contextual family, but it is broader and more duplication-prone than c01-c03, with medium leakage and runtime risk, sparse-category noise, and weak validation evidence.
Cheap and isolated, but chronological minibatching has no direct positive evidence and may introduce recency bias; expected gain is very small with low confidence.
Low-cost regularization test with low leakage and runtime risk, but the direction is uncertain, the expected gain is minimal, and the supplied evidence does not specifically support this change.
Feasible and low risk, but display dimensions have no positive screening evidence, likely affect calibration more than ordering, and have very low confidence and expected gain.
Novel interaction modeling could help, but it duplicates c04's architectural direction while adding higher runtime risk, sparse-ID volatility, low confidence, and a wide possible downside.
Useful only as a diagnostic negative control; removing user identity is expected to harm within-user ordering and offers essentially no prospect of winning the scarce experiment.
A sanity control rather than a recommender improvement: user-only scores cannot differentiate items within a user and are expected to collapse both ranking metrics.
